items.longBusinessSummary: Nebius Group N.V., a technology company, engages in building full-stack infrastructure to service the global AI industry in the United States, the United Kingdom, and internationally. It offers Nebius builds full-stack infrastructure for AI, including large-scale GPU clusters, cloud platforms, and tools and services for developers. The company also provides TripleTen, an edtech platform for re-skilling individuals for careers in technolgy; and Avride, which develops autonomous driving technology for self-driving cars and delivery robotics. It has a strategic alliance with NVIDIA Corporation to support the expansion of the company's AI cloud infrastructure. The company was formerly known as Yandex N.V. and changed its name to Nebius Group N.V. in August 2024. Nebius Group N.V. was founded in 1989 and is based in Schiphol, the Netherlands.

Title: CLS Stock Soars Premarket After Blowout Q3 — Retail Calls It ‘Very Inexpensive’ As Celestica Touts AI ‘Supercycle’
Author: Deepti Sri   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 9:17 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T08:17:54+00:00
=== BODY ===
Q3 revenue jumped 83% to $5.83 billion, while adjusted EPS more than doubled to $3.30.
Celestica forecasts $40 billion in 2027 revenue, above Wall Street expectations.
The company raised its 2026 sales and earnings targets but cut its free-cash-flow forecast.
Celestica (CLS) shares surged 17% in premarket trading on Tuesday as stronger-than-expected earnings and an upbeat AI demand outlook fueled retail bets that the market is still undervaluing the data center infrastructure company's growth prospects.
CLS stock fell 5% on Monday to $246.65, with shares on track to post their worst month in over 6 years.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
The rally offers a bright spot in a bruised AI trade, with CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN each down more than 35% so far in October as investors question whether future revenue can justify the cost of their infrastructure buildouts.
Celestica beat expectations as third-quarter (Q3) revenue jumped 83% to $5.83 billion and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) more than doubled to $3.30. Analysts had expected $5.47 billion in sales and EPS of $2.96.
Connectivity & Cloud Solutions powered the growth, with revenue doubling to $4.87 billion, while the company's adjusted operating margin hit a record 8.5%. Celestica expects that momentum to accelerate. Its 2027 outlook calls for $40 billion in revenue, up 90% from this year's updated forecast and above the $35.71 billion consensus estimate. It also targets adjusted EPS of $21.50 and a record adjusted operating margin of 9%.
"Celestica is well-positioned to continue to support leading hyperscalers and frontier AI labs through the ongoing AI infrastructure supercycle," CEO Rob Mionis said.
The company's confidence also stretches beyond 2027. "The demand environment continues to be very robust, supporting our 2027 revenue outlook, with customer demand forecasts meaningfully higher for 2028," Mionis said.
Celestica raised its 2026 revenue target to $21 billion from $20.5 billion and its adjusted EPS forecast to $11.55 from $11.30.
However, it cut its free-cash-flow outlook to $460 million from $600 million, citing working-capital investments to support next year's expansion. Capex is expected to hit $1.5 billion to $2 billion in 2027.
Stocktwits sentiment for CLS was 'extremely bullish' amid a whopping 38,500% surge in 24-hour message volumes.
One user said, "2027 outlook looks very strong. Stock looks very inexpensive at current levels!" Another user said, "Short-term price action on a lot of these AI stocks has generated some extremely favorable valuations."
A separate user argued, "A 20 forward PE places us over $400 per share. would be priced for perfection but these guys deserve it." Meanwhile, another user said, "AI Earnings haven't been the issue. Its about sustainability out further than 6 months."
CLS stock has declined 17% year-to-date.

Title: MU, SKHY Stocks Rise As Anthropic Filing Shows $450B In Compute Commitments; Kospi Rally Triggers Program-Trading Pause
Author: Yuvraj Malik   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 8:13 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T07:13:32+00:00
=== BODY ===
Micron rose 1% in overnight trading, while the South Korea Bull 3X ETF gained nearly 3%.
Neoclouds stocks recovered as well, with CoreWeave and Nebius gaining about 0.5% each.
Anthropic made its S-1 filing public on Monday, showing plans to spend $450 billion in cloud computing agreements over the next 7-10 years.
Memory stocks rose after Anthropic's IPO filing, with gains spreading to Asian markets as investors weighed the AI company's surging revenue and compute commitments alongside its large losses.
Micron (MU) stock rose 1% in overnight trading ahead of Tuesday, while Seoul shares of SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics gained 5.6% and 4%, respectively, on Tuesday.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
South Korea's Kospi was up 3% at the time of writing. Earlier, the Korea Exchange triggered a "sidecar," a brief pause in program trading that kicks in when futures move sharply. The Direxion Daily South Korea Bull 3X ETF (KORU) rose 2.8% in overnight trading.
Neocloud stocks also recovered, with CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) gaining about 0.5% each overnight, while cloud giant Alphabet (GOOGL) was up 0.3%. Nvidia (NVDA), Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Amazon (AMZN) and Microsoft (MSFT) were in the red after gains in Monday's regular session.
Anthropic made its S-1 filing public on Monday, showing first-half revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.16 billion in H1 2025. The company reported a net loss of $80.7 billion, largely driven by a $72.4 billion accounting charge related to convertible notes.
However, Anthropic's long-term purchase commitments, which flow through to cloud and AI infrastructure providers, caught investors' attention.
The AI company would spend $450 billion in cloud computing agreements over the next seven to ten years, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing the filing. It plans to spend $111 billion on Google cloud computing contracts, $110 billion with Amazon Web Services, and $31 billion on Microsoft, "regardless of actual usage."
Anthropic will also spend up to $86 billion renting Nvidia chips from smaller AI cloud providers Nscale and Lambda through 2033 and 2034, respectively, in addition to other cloud deals, the Journal reported.
Anthropic's financials drew broadly positive comments from analysts and investors, with some praising its pace of growth and deep customer spread.
Anthropic will go public on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT," according to the S-1. The company reportedly plans to list its shares in the week of Nov. 16, the Journal reported separately, citing people familiar with the matter.
On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for ANTHZZX and KORU jumped to 'extremely bullish' from 'neutral' the previous day, while sentiment for OpenAI (OPEAZZX) shifted to 'bearish' from 'neutral.'
The sentiment was 'bullish' for SKHY and 'bearish' for MU. Investors will now turn to quarterly reports from a series of memory chipmakers, Seagate (STX) on Tuesday, SK Hynix on Wednesday, and Samsung on Thursday, for further clues on the chip trade.
